text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on January 5 in history.
1066 - Edward the Confessor, king of England from 1042, died. He was canonized in 1161.
1477 - Charles the Bold was defeated and killed by the Swiss at the Battle of Nancy in the Swiss-Burgundian Wars.
1589 - Catherine de Medici, wife of King Henry II of France, died. Daughter of Lorenzo de Medici, she became regent of France from 1560 after the death of her husband.
1592 - Shah Jahan born. Mughal emperor from 1628, he had the Taj Mahal built in memory of his favourite queen Mumtaz Mahal.
1757 - Jean-Francois Damiens attempted to assassinate Louis XV of France as he was entering his carriage at Versailles. He was later executed.
1762 - Elizabeth, Empress of Russia, died and was succeeded by her nephew Peter III.
1855 - King Camp Gillette, U.S. inventor of the safety razor, born.

1876 - Konrad Adenauer, West German statesman, born. First chancellor of the Federal Republic of Germany from 1949 (to 1963), he presided over the rebuilding of West Germany after its destruction in World War Two.
1919 - Spartacists in Berlin led by Rosa Luxemburg and Karl Liebknecht attempted to take over the government and seized a number of buildings.
1922 - Sir Ernest Henry Shackleton, explorer, died. He made several expeditions to the Antarctic and died on the Falkland Islands before another Antarctic mission
1925 - Nellie Taylor Ross took up her post as governor of Wyoming and became the first woman governor of a state.

1933 - Calvin Coolidge, 30th U.S. president, died. He was governor of Massachusetts and became vice-president in 1921. He succeeded as president on Warren Harding's death in 1923 and was elected in 1924.
1938 - King Juan Carlos I, born. Groomed by Francisco Franco to inherit the right-wing dictatorship, he steered Spain to democracy and turned the sceptical into monarchists.
1941 - Amy Johnson, aviator, died. The first woman to fly solo from England to Australia in 1930, her body was never found, after she crashed in the Thames estuary.
1964 - Pope Paul VI and Patriarch Athenagoras I met in Jerusalem, the first meeting of the leaders of the Roman Catholic and Orthodox churches since the fifteenth century.

1968 - In Czechoslovakia, Alexander Dubcek succeeded Antonin Novotny as First Secretary of the Communist Party. His policy of democracy within a Communist framework led to the occupation of Czechoslovakia by the Soviet Union.
1969 - Soviet interplanetary spacecraft Venus 5 was launched. Five days later, Venus 6 was launched. They reached Venus on May 16 and 17 respectively.

1993 - Oil poured onto the coast of northern Scotland's Shetland Islands after the 89,000-tonne Liberian-registered Braer hit rocks in heavy seas. The tanker carried 84,500 tonnes of crude oil. A huge oil slick stretched 25 miles up the coast.
1994 - Former U.S. House of Representatives Speaker Thomas "Tip" O'Neill, a Democratic party stalwart whose political career spanned nine presidencies, died in Boston.
1996 - In Russia, Foreign Minister Andrei Kozyrev, admired in the West but reviled by Russian conservatives, resigned.
1996 - Japan's Prime Minister Tomiichi Murayama announced his resignation in a surprise move.
1996 - Yahya Ayyash, the "Engineer", the elusive mastermind behind a wave of Islamic suicide bombings against Israel, was killed in Gaza, apparently by a booby-trapped cellular telephone.
